The geap library solves general equilibrium asset pricing models in
Python. You specify preferences and a consumption process, and you
attach cash-flow claims. You then solve the model so that the growth
forecast and the discount rate come from the same economy.

The model families share [`AssetPricingModel`](lrr/api.qmd). Long-run
risks uses Epstein-Zin preferences and a consumption process with
persistent growth. Power utility is the two-state CCAPM of Mehra and
Prescott (1985), and habit is the Campbell and Cochrane (1999) model
with external surplus consumption.

| Family | Estimator | What it does |
|:---|:---|:---|
| [Long-run risks](lrr/index.qmd) | [`LongRunRisksModel`](lrr/api.qmd) | Prices named dividend claims on a consumption process with persistent growth |
| [Power utility](ccapm/index.qmd) | [`PowerUtilityModel`](ccapm/api.qmd) | Two-state consumption chain, power kernel, and levered claims |
| [Habit](habit/index.qmd) | [`CampbellCochraneModel`](habit/api.qmd) | External habit, surplus consumption, and i.i.d. consumption growth |
| [GMM](gmm/index.qmd) | [`geap.gmm`](gmm/api.qmd) | Hansen GMM on pricing errors and linear factor means |

```python
import geap

model = geap.LongRunRisksModel()
res = model.solve()
print(res.summary())
res.compare("value", "growth", market="market").premium
```

The default calibration is Table II of Kiku (2006). Average returns are
not used in the cash-flow step, and the premium is therefore a
prediction from the solved economy.

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
import geap
import pandas as pd
from great_tables import GT

KIKU_GT = dict(table_background_color="transparent", table_font_size="0.92rem",
               heading_title_font_size="1.05rem", heading_subtitle_font_size="0.85rem",
               source_notes_font_size="0.8rem", column_labels_font_weight="bold",
               data_row_padding="4px")

model = geap.LongRunRisksModel()
sim = model.simulate(n_samples=300, years=74, seed=0)
vg = sim.compare("value", "growth", market="market")

data_er = {"growth": 7.81, "value": 13.88, "market": 8.56}   # Kiku, Table I
names = ("growth", "value", "market")
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "claim": names,
    "data": [data_er[k] for k in names],
    "model": [sim.expected_returns[k] for k in names],
})
(
    GT(df)
    .tab_header(title="Average annual returns, data and long-run risks")
    .cols_label(claim="", data="E[R] data (%)", model="E[R] model (%)")
    .fmt_number(columns=["data", "model"], decimals=2)
    .tab_source_note(f"Value minus growth is about 6 points in the data "
                     f"(Kiku, Table I) and {vg.premium:.1f} points in the model.")
    .tab_source_note(f"The CAPM beta ratio of value to growth is "
                     f"{vg.beta_ratio:.2f}.")
    .tab_options(**KIKU_GT)
)
```

::: {.firewall}
The code cell computes the model column at build time from the Table II
calibration, and the data numbers are from Kiku (2006), Table I.
:::
